item.title: Mercedes crowned 2026 F1 constructors' champion at Brazilian GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes has won the 2026 Formula 1 constructors' championship, sealing the title at the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos. Antonelli and Russell started second and seventh on the grid, after the Briton took a five-place grid penalty. While Antonelli took the lead from polesitter Lando Norris at the start of the race and extended his lead to five seconds over the first seven laps, he later spun into Turn 1, giving Norris the opportunity to retake the position. Antonelli started to drop down the order as he complained that "the car is pulling on one side when accelerating." After heavy rainfall in the closing laps of the race, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell finished fourth and fifth, which was enough to put the team out of reach of Ferrari, whose drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finished seventh and ninth, respectively. Lando Norris won the Brazilian Grand Prix and the McLaren driver was joined on the podium by Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Mercedes arrived in Sao Paulo 126 points clear of Ferrari and needed to leave with a lead of 129 points. The title completes a championship double for the team, one week after Antonelli clinched the drivers' crown at the Mexican Grand Prix to become the youngest world champion in the history of F1. The 2026 title is the Brackley outfit's ninth constructors' championship, after already winning in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021. item.title: Man Utd rescue Villa draw with incredible fightback, Chelsea stunned
item.description: Manchester United defender Patrick Dorgu (2nd R) celebrates after scoring against Aston Villa (Darren Staples) Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of avoiding the sack, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday. United boss Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal. But Carrick's side struck twice in the six minutes of additional time through Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to leave their manager's future still uncertain. United are in the relegation zone and have not won in their last eight Premier League matches, so it is far from sure that Carrick will survive the axe. He had earned a stay of execution when United's hierarchy allowed him to remain in charge despite last weekend's loss at Chelsea. United responded by ending a nine-match winless run in all competitions as they came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. But United, who have only three wins in 15 games this season, were back in turmoil when they fell 2-0 down against Villa in the first four minutes at Old Trafford. Alysson struck in the first minute with a shot that squirmed under United keeper Senne Lammens. Nicolas Jackson slotted in the second three minutes later after a weak save from Lammens pushed the ball into his path. Bruno Fernandes got one back with a 16th-minute penalty after Boubacar Kamara fouled Matheus Cunha before former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans slammed in United's 44th-minute equaliser. Villa's John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty following Diogo Dalot's clumsy challenge on Alysson. Leon Goretzka poked in Villa's fourth from close-range after United's Leny Yoro headed against his own crossbar in the 53rd minute. Yet Zirkzee's stoppage-time finish gave United hope and Dorgu headed their dramatic equaliser in the final seconds after a weak punch from Villa keeper Zion Suzuki. Carrick wore a bewildered look on his face as he walked down the tunnel towards an uncertain future, with United next in action at Liverpool on November 22. Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish. Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season. Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso. - Liverpool back on track - Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill. "We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there," Alonso said. Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win at lowly Crystal Palace.

item.title: Hamza Zahoor's century overshadows Arjun Rajput's 107 as Pakistan U19 pull off thrilling three-wicket win over India
item.description: Pakistan Under-19 pulled off a memorable three-wicket victory over arch-rivals India in the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026, with captain Hamza Zahoor producing a composed century to guide his side home in a tense chase at Al Amerat, Oman, on Sunday. Chasing 209, Pakistan found themselves in deep trouble at 63/5, with India's bowlers threatening to take the game away. However, Zahoor held his nerve and led a remarkable recovery, stitching together a crucial 107-run partnership with Hasnain Abbas Dar to turn the contest around. Dar contributed 38 off 67 balls before departing at 168/6, giving India another opening. But Zahoor continued to anchor the chase, eventually taking Pakistan across the finish line with three wickets to spare. The result handed Pakistan an important Group A victory over their traditional rivals and strengthened their position in the race for a place in the semi-finals. Arjun Rajput's fighting century rescues India Earlier, India endured a disastrous start after captain Lakshya Raichandani was dismissed for a duck in the first over. Pakistan's pace attack kept the pressure on, reducing India to 42/4 and then 86/5. With the top order back in the pavilion, Arjun Rajput took responsibility and launched a counter-attack. The left-hander smashed 107 off 85 deliveries, striking 11 fours and five sixes, to give India a fighting total. Rajput found useful support from Anvay Dravid (10) and Manal Chauhan (11), but his dismissal at 170/7 in the 36th over triggered another collapse. India lost their remaining wickets for 38 runs and were bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs. Kavya Patel's 23 provided a late contribution, helping India cross the 200-run mark. Pakistan bowlers keep India under control Pakistan's bowling unit played a major role in restricting India to 208. Ali Raza led the attack with three wickets, while Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq also claimed three wickets apiece. The early strikes from Raza and the pressure maintained by Mohammad Sayyam put India on the back foot, before the spinners tightened their grip in the middle overs. India fight back but Zahoor stands firm India did not make Pakistan's chase easy. Manal Chauhan picked up two wickets, while Kavya Patel and Mohit Ulva also struck as Pakistan slipped to 61/5. But Zahoor's partnership with Dar changed the course of the match. Even after Dar's dismissal, the Pakistan captain remained in control and completed the job, sealing a three-wicket win for his side.

item.title: Mercedes clinches F1 Constructors’ Championship
item.description: (Photo by Alfredo ESTRELLA / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The worst-kept secret in the Formula 1 paddock a year ago was that Mercedes would be on the front foot this year, with the arrival of sweeping new technical regulations. That secret has fully materialized on this day at the São Paulo Grand Prix. A week after Kimi Antonelli clinched the Drivers’ Championship, the team secured the Constructors’ title at the São Paulo Grand Prix. While Lando Norris took the win at Interlagos, and the Red Bull duo of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar took the other two podium spots, the Silver Arrows got the results they needed from Antonelli and George Russell to clinch the team’s ninth Constructors’ Championship. Russell crossed the finish line in P4, while Antonelli took the checkered flag down in P5. The day began with Mercedes needing to outscore Ferrari by just three points to wrap up the team’s eighth Constructors’ Championship, and with both Antonelli and Russell starting inside the top ten — and Ferrari’s duo of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc starting at the back of the grid due to engine penalties — the door was open for the Silver Arrows to wrap things up at Interlagos. However, it was not without some drama. The race began with the field on the intermediate tires, due to wet conditions in São Paulo. Both Antonelli and Russell endured some tense moments in those wet conditions, with Antonelli spinning out of the lead in the early stages, and Russell spinning as well as he exited pit lane during a pit stop to switch over from the intermediate tires to the C5 softs. Mercedes stabilized things with both drivers running inside the top five on Lap 56, but Interlagos is known for dealing some wild cards each year. And one more was looming, as dark clouds returned and drivers were being warned that heavier rain was on the horizon for the final laps. On Lap 57, the rain arrived. Mercedes warned Antonelli that the intensity of the rain might require a stop for intermediate tires once more. The newly crowned Drivers’ Champion was all over the rear wing of Isack Hadjar for the final podium spot, pushing the Red Bull driver lap after lap as conditions worsened in the rain. Both drivers started to wobble on Lap 62, and some drivers at the back of the field made the early gamble for intermediates, including Fernando Alonso, Leclerc, Liam Lawson, and even Russell. Then Norris pitted from the lead on Lap 62, making the switch to the intermediates as well. Max Verstappen followed from P2, and both Hadjar and Antonelli made the same decision as well. When the field stabilized, Mercedes instructed Antonelli to let Russell through into P4, releasing the veteran to try and chase down a podium spot so the Silver Arrows could celebrate in style. item.title: Aggies Underdogs At Home Against Tennessee
item.description: Texas A&M was competitive against South Carolina, but the Aggies ultimately were unable to find victory as they fell to the Gamecocks 17-9. Now Texas A&M will return to Kyle Field to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Per FanDuel , the Aggies are 2.5-point underdogs when Tennessee comes to town. The over / under is set at 42.5 points. Tennessee was dominant last time out as the Volunteers thrashed Kentucky 34-6. UT is 7-2 on the season, with the losses coming at home against Texas and on the road against South Carolina. The Volunteers lead the all-time series against the Aggies 3-2. The last time Tennessee came to College Station was in 2016, when the Aggies won a thriller over the Vols 45-38. That contest was also the first trip Tennessee ever made to Kyle Field. Texas A&M only being a 2.5-point underdog against Tennessee this week comes as a bit of a surprise to me, given the recent performances turned in by both teams, but maybe Vegas knows something we don’t. If Mike Elko and the Aggies are going to go bowling this year, they will need to find a way to win two of the next three contests. We’ll see if Texas A&M can pull off a shocker at Kyle Field.

item.title: Magic Johnson celebrates huge milestone in HIV journey
item.description: Magic Johnson celebrates huge milestone in HIV journey appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Magic Johnson is celebrating a major milestone with his HIV diagnosis over 30 years ago. The retired NBA legend held a press conference in 1991 when he announced that he had been diagnosed with HIV. On Saturday, Nov. 7, Johnson shared that he is thankful for how far he’s come since his original announcement. “Look at how far God has brought me since my HIV announcement 35 years ago! It is truly because of His grace and mercy that I am still here and thriving,” Johnson wrote on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “God never gave up on me, and I kept the faith,” he continued. “I am thankful for all of the prayers from my family, friends, and fans throughout the years, and I am a living witness that there’s nothing too hard for God.” Johnson learned of his diagnosis when he went to get a physical ahead of the 1991-92 NBA season. When he heard of the diagnosis for the first time, he told CBS Mornings in 2024 that he was “devastated.” His wife, Earletha “Cookie” Johnson,” was pregnant at the time and while their son, Earvin “EJ” Johnson III was found HIV-negative, he shared that telling her the news was difficult. “It was hard because I loved her so much and I hated to hurt her,” he said. He didn’t play a regular-season game that year but he did perform in the NBA All-Star team in 1992 when fans voted him in for a spot on the roster. “It proved to be the right decision,” he said. “It helped people who were living with not just HIV and AIDS, but with any disease, that you can live on, you can be — live a productive life.” Since he learned of his own diagnosis, he has had made a huge difference in supporting those who have been diagnosed with HIV/AIDS. He started the Magic Johnson Foundation to help others with their fight against the virus. The foundation has provided more than 40,000 free HIV screenings nationwide. It also partnered with the AIDS Healthcare Foundation to create HIV/AIDS clinics in California and Florida. The foundation also has created the Earvin Johnson Sr. scholarship program to aid students at Michigan State University. item.title: Wisconsin Badgers Secure Bowl Spot With 31-10 Win
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Madison, Wisconsin, USA; Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Ryan Hopkins (10) celebrates after throwing a touchdown pass during the fourth quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Camp Randall Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The Wisconsin Badgers officially secured a spot in a bowl game after a dominant 31-10 victory over Rutgers on Saturday. item.description: Heat's Erik Spoelstra takes massive shot at Doc Rivers for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat entered the offseason with a mission to acquire some big names who could help position the organization for success this season and potentially beyond. Miami made several significant moves that had fans excited about what the team could accomplish. The biggest move of them all was acquiring an NBA champion. The Heat pulled off a blockbuster trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo. “The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks (including No. 13 in Tuesday's NBA draft), one pick swap and one second-round pick, sources told ESPN. The start of the season has brought some challenges for Antetokounmpo, particularly after his former head coach, Doc Rivers, recently made some critical comments about what it was like coaching him. Rivers described the two-time MVP as a difficult player to coach. “He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it,” Rivers said. Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra wasn't going to let those comments go unanswered. He responded to Rivers, making it clear that Antetokounmpo's development is now Miami's responsibility. “Look, I like Doc, and I respect him, this is our business now. We went into the season thinking that that would be a process, playing with somebody (Giannis) that commands so much attention. That’s a different style than some of the guys that have come here, that have played before,” Spoelstra said. There is no doubt that Miami is going to stand behind its major offseason addition, but it is rare to see Spoelstra publicly respond to another coach in this manner. The Heat view Antetokounmpo as a cornerstone of the organization, and Spoelstra is making it clear that the team is committed to helping him succeed. Spoelstra understands that the season is far from over and isn't going to let outside criticism become a distraction for his team. A head coach is naturally going to stand behind his players, and Spoelstra has made it clear that Antetokounmpo has his full support. item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez has revealed a change in approach as he looks to seal the MotoGP world championship when the series returns to Europe in two weeks. While both Aprilias are still in mathematical contention, Martin remains a long shot, while Bezzecchi, in his own words, "needs a miracle". But the job is not officially done for Marquez. A win in the sprint at Portimao will certainly be enough for Marquez to wrap up the title. But Marc might be able secure the crown with only a middling result in the sprint - depending on what his opponents do. Fans felt outraged, but front offices focused on a heated debate over Brown’s true value on the court. This debate centered on how modern data analysis of players in a league flooded with information works. Brown is a five-time All-Star and a former Finals MVP who finished sixth in regular-season MVP voting in 2026 after averaging a career-best 28.7 points per game, according to ESPN . Despite these impressive traditional numbers, advanced statistics were more skeptical of his stardom. Teams track points, rebounds, assists, shot quality, pick-and-roll frequency, and isolation efficiency. While individual data points are nearly endless, the objective remains the same. A front office should identify players who help the team outscore opponents rather than players who just collect strong statistics in a vacuum. Players boasting top individual stats frequently deliver the greatest winning impact, though this is not always the case.
